She married a stranger she met hitchhiking. Then she used the wedding to rob her own family.
Shanghai. Meng's small property agency has failed.
So she asks the driver who gave her a lift to play her husband. He's already married. He says yes.
At the wedding, she tells her relatives: he's a big property developer.
His connections, she says, can get them new flats twenty percent cheaper.
To prove it, she sells her cousin a flat at half price. The cousin spreads the word.
The relatives pay. Some even sell the homes they live in.
Years pass. No flats. These discounts take time, she says.
Then she hands them keys. They move in. They decorate.
But there are no ownership papers. Temporarily impossible, she says.
Then one relative calls the developer. The flat isn't hers. It's rented.
Meng had rented every flat. The total: twelve million yuan.
The court: twelve and a half years for Meng. Six for the fake husband. Five for the cousin who spread the word.
Her own family. Would you have checked the papers?
